text: To improve the agent’s performance and fully address the need, new demonstrations should be created where the agent begins right next to fire hazards, either on the left or right side. These demonstrations should clearly show the agent deliberately moving away from the nearby fire by choosing safe corridors, such as the left-edge, top-edge, or right-column paths, instead of moving straight toward the goal and risking collision. It’s important to include varied goal locations to show that the strategy is about local hazard avoidance first, not just greedy moves toward the goal. Each demonstration should have clear annotations explaining why the agent chooses an initial safe step away from fire before heading toward the goal. This approach will help the agent learn to prioritize immediate safety by selecting hazard-free routes close to the start, which reduces collisions and improves its ability to generalize in environments with randomly placed fires and goals.
